source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

56027.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Byrd and Hageman, Niobrara County stayed overwhelmingly Republican but shifted 8 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 81 points in 2024; Hageman won it 800 to 125, a 73-point margin. That was a smaller swing than the typical Wyoming county (12 points) and the statewide move (16 points). Every county in the state moved left, and Niobrara ranks 19th of 23 by size of move. It cast the fewest votes of any Wyoming county. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Crook 6 points, Weston 9, Converse 12.

Only 925 votes were cast, 75% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56045.t:
Weston County stayed overwhelmingly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, where Hageman beat Byrd 2,077 to 395, a margin of 68 points. That is a 9-point move toward the Democrats from Trump's 77-point win here in 2024. Every Wyoming county moved left, but Weston's shift was smaller than the typical county's 12 points and the state's 16, ranking 17th of 23. Among similar counties, Crook moved 6 points, Converse 12 and Campbell 13.

Only 2,472 votes were cast, 71% of the 2024 total, with 99% of the expected vote counted. Because so many fewer people voted, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56015.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Goshen County gave Republican Harriet Hageman 3,539 votes to Democrat James Byrd's 966, a margin of 57 points. That is 4 points narrower than Donald Trump's 61-point win over Kamala Harris here in 2024. It was still the smallest shift toward the Democrats of any of Wyoming's 23 counties, all of which moved left. The typical county in the state moved 12 points and the state as a whole 16. Counties of similar size and 2024 margin moved further: Sublette 15 points, Carbon 14 and Hot Springs 9.

Some 4,505 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot show whether the shift came from voters changing their minds or from some staying home.

56043.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Washakie County backed Republican Harriet Hageman over Democrat James Byrd by 2,161 votes to 602, a margin of 56 points. That is 8 points narrower than Trump's 64-point margin here in 2024, a smaller shift than Wyoming's 16-point move statewide, where Hageman won by 31. Every Wyoming county moved left, the typical one by 12 points, and Washakie ranks 20th of 23. Similar counties moved by similar amounts: Platte by 7 points, Johnson by 9, Uinta by 13.

Turnout was 2,763 votes, 72% of the 3,841 cast in 2024. With that drop, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56039.t:
Teton County, already the most Democratic-leaning place in this comparison, moved further left in the U.S. Senate race. Byrd beat Hageman here 7,557 to 2,744, a margin of 47 points, up from Harris's 35-point edge over Trump in 2024. That 11-point shift is a bit smaller than the typical Wyoming county's 12 and the statewide move of 16, and it trails similar counties Albany (+20), Laramie (+18) and Fremont (+14). All 23 Wyoming counties moved left, though Hageman still won statewide.

Turnout fell to 10,301 votes, 79% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56003.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Big Horn County stayed overwhelmingly Republican but shifted about 12 points toward the Democrats. Hageman beat Byrd here 3,297 to 805, a margin of R+61, compared with Trump's R+73 in 2024. That is close to the typical Wyoming county's move of 12 points. All 23 of the state's counties moved left, and Wyoming as a whole went from R+46 to R+31. Similar counties moved by comparable amounts: Converse by 12 points, Lincoln by 10 and Weston by 9.

Turnout fell sharply. The county cast 4,102 votes, 72% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56033.t:
Sheridan County moved 16 points toward the Democrats in Wyoming's U.S. Senate race, where Republican Harriet Hageman beat Democrat James Byrd. Donald Trump carried the county by 50 points in 2024; Hageman won it by 34, with 8,073 votes to Byrd's 3,966. That is about the same as the statewide shift of 16 points, and larger than the typical Wyoming county's 12 or the typical national county's 14. All 23 Wyoming counties moved left, and Sheridan ranks fifth by size of move.

Turnout was 74% of the 2024 total, with 12,039 votes cast against 16,219, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Sweetwater and Natrona moved more, and Park moved less.

56009.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Converse County gave Republican Harriet Hageman 3,515 votes to Democrat James Byrd's 846, a margin of 61 points. In the 2024 presidential race, Trump carried the county by 74 points, so it moved 12 points toward the Democrats. That matches the typical Wyoming county, where all 23 moved left, and is slightly less than the statewide shift of 16 points in a race Hageman won by 31.

Only 4,361 votes were cast, 65% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Big Horn moved 12 points, Weston 9 and Crook 6.

56005.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Republican Harriet Hageman carried Campbell County over Democrat James Byrd by 9,095 votes to 2,025, a margin of 63 points. Trump had won the county by 77 points in 2024, so it moved 14 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the typical Wyoming county (13 points) and in line with the typical county nationally (14). All 23 Wyoming counties moved left. Campbell's shift was larger than those of the similar counties Weston (9 points) and Crook (6) and close to Converse's (13).

Turnout fell to 11,168 votes, 61% of the 18,236 cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56013.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Fremont County voted for Republican Harriet Hageman over Democrat James Byrd by 7,981 to 4,936, a margin of 24 points. Trump carried the county by 37 points in 2024, so it moved 14 points toward the Democrats. That is a little more than the typical Wyoming county, which moved 12 points, and a little less than the state as a whole, which moved 16. Among similar counties, Laramie moved 18 points, Sheridan 16 and Natrona 19.

The county cast 12,917 votes, 76% of the 17,060 it cast in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56029.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Democrat Byrd and Republican Hageman, Park County went for Hageman 8,701 to 3,153, a margin of 47 points. Trump had carried it by 59 points in 2024, so the county moved about 13 points toward the Democrats, close to the typical Wyoming county's 12-point move and a little under the national typical shift of 14. Every county in the state moved left.

Only 11,854 votes were cast, 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Carbon moved 14 points, Goshen 4 and Sweetwater 22.

56019.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Byrd and Hageman, Johnson County moved 9 points toward the Democrats. Trump carried it by 64 points in 2024. Hageman won it by 55, 2,747 votes to 804. That is a smaller shift than Wyoming's 16-point statewide move and the typical county's 12 points in a state where all 23 counties moved left. Johnson ranks 18th of 23 by move. Similar counties were mixed: Washakie moved 8 points, Platte 7 and Uinta 13.

Only 3,551 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56007.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Carbon County gave Republican Harriet Hageman 3,060 votes to 1,188 for Democrat James Byrd, a 44-point margin. Donald Trump carried it by 58 points in 2024, so the county moved 14 points toward the Democrats. That is a bit more than the typical Wyoming county's 12-point shift and matches the typical move nationally, though slightly less than the state's 16-point swing. All 23 Wyoming counties moved left. Sublette and Park, similar in their 2024 vote, moved 15 and 13 points, while Goshen moved 4.

Only 4,248 votes were cast, 67% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56037.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Sweetwater County shifted further toward the Democrats than any other county in Wyoming. Donald Trump carried it by 53 points in 2024; this time Republican Harriet Hageman won it by 32, taking 7,241 votes to 3,766 for Democrat James Byrd. That 22-point move toward the Democrats compares with 16 points in Sheridan, 13 in Park and 19 in Natrona, and with a typical move of 12 points across the state, where all 23 counties moved left.

Turnout fell sharply, to 11,007 votes from 16,569 in 2024, about two-thirds of the earlier total. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56017.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Hot Springs County voted for Republican Harriet Hageman over Democrat James Byrd 1,577 to 501, a margin of 52 points. That is 9 points closer than Trump's 61-point win here in 2024. Every Wyoming county moved toward the Democrats, and this one moved less than most, ranking 16th of 23, against a typical county shift of 12 points and a statewide swing of 16. Among similar counties, Sublette moved 15 points, Washakie 8 and Goshen 4.

The county cast 2,078 votes, 80% of its 2024 total and the second-smallest count in the state. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56023.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Lincoln County, Wyoming, gave Hageman (R) 5,835 votes to Byrd's (D) 1,526, a Republican margin of 59 points. That is 10 points closer than Trump's 68-point margin here in 2024. But only 7,361 votes were cast, 69% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Every Wyoming county moved left. Lincoln's shift was smaller than the typical county's 12 points, the statewide 16 and the national typical 14. Among similar counties, Uinta moved 13 points and Big Horn 12, while Platte moved 7. Hageman won the state by 31 points.

56001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Albany County flipped from Trump to the Democrat. James Byrd beat Harriet Hageman here by 17 points, 7,675 votes to 5,448, after Trump had carried it by 3 points in 2024. That swing of about 20 points toward the Democrats was the second-largest among Wyoming's 23 counties, all of which moved left, against a typical shift of 12 points statewide and 14 nationally. No other Wyoming county changed hands.

Turnout fell to 13,123 votes, 74% of the 17,639 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Laramie moved 18 points, Fremont 14 and Teton 11.

56031.t:
Platte County stayed deeply Republican in the U.S. Senate race, with Hageman beating Byrd 2,789 to 727, a margin of about 59 points. That is a shift of roughly 7 points toward the Democrats from Trump's 66-point margin here in 2024. All 23 Wyoming counties moved left, but Platte ranks 21st by size of move, trailing the typical Wyoming county (+12) and the statewide shift (+16). Similar counties moved more: Johnson about 9 points, Washakie 8 and Uinta 13.

Only 3,516 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56025.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Natrona County voted for Hageman over Byrd 14,246 to 7,690, a Republican margin of 30 points. Trump had carried it by 49 points in 2024, so the county moved 19 points toward the Democrats. That was the third-largest shift among Wyoming's 23 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Wyoming county moved 12 points, the state as a whole 16, and the typical county nationally 14. Among similar Wyoming counties, Sweetwater moved 22 points, Sheridan 16 and Park 13.

Turnout was far below 2024: 21,936 votes, 65% of the 33,591 cast then. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56035.t:
Sublette County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race but shifted noticeably toward the Democrats. Harriet Hageman beat James Byrd 2,657 to 989, a margin of about 46 points, down from Trump's 61-point margin in 2024. That 15-point move roughly matches the statewide shift of 16 points and ranks sixth among Wyoming's 23 counties, all of which moved left. The typical Wyoming county moved 12 points, and the typical county nationally moved 14.

Turnout was 3,646 votes, 75% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Sublette moved more than counties with similar 2024 results and size: Goshen moved 4 points, Hot Springs 9 and Johnson 9.

56011.t:
Crook County stayed overwhelmingly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, with Hageman beating Byrd 2,659 to 427, a margin of 72 points. That is about 6 points less Republican than Trump's 78-point margin over Harris in 2024. Every Wyoming county moved toward the Democrats, but Crook moved less than all but one of the 23. The typical county shifted 12 points and the state as a whole 16. Nearby Weston, Converse and Campbell, which voted much like Crook in 2024, moved 9 to 13 points.

Only 3,086 votes were cast, 72% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

56021.t:
Laramie County, Wyoming's largest by votes cast, swung 18 points toward the Democrats in the U.S. Senate race between Harriet Hageman and James Byrd. Trump carried it by 32 points in 2024; Hageman won it by 14, with 17,258 votes to 12,919. That is the fourth-largest move among Wyoming's 23 counties, all of which shifted left, and above both the typical county statewide (12 points) and nationally (14 points). Natrona moved by a similar amount (19 points), Sheridan by 16 and Fremont by 14.

Turnout fell to 30,177 votes, 70% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

56041.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Uinta County voted for Republican Harriet Hageman over Democrat James Byrd 4,658 to 1,512, a margin of 51 points. In 2024 Trump carried it by 64, so the county moved 13 points toward the Democrats. That is slightly more than the typical Wyoming county (12) and a bit less than the state as a whole (16) or the typical county nationally (14). It ranks 10th of Wyoming's 23 counties by move.

Turnout was 69% of the 2024 vote, 6,170 ballots against 8,984, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Uinta shifted further than similar counties such as Johnson (9 points), Washakie (8) and Goshen (4).
